verdict:
**B — fragility is entirely confined to rounds that had already declared themselves not clean.**
  **6/35 scripts flip on a single-item drop** (overall cell rate 0.058 over 171 cells), and the split by the round's OWN verdict is total:
    · `ALL GATES PASS` — **12 scripts, 0 flip, mean rate 0.000**
    · `UNVERIFIED`    — 12 scripts, 3 flip
    · `OVERTURNED`    — 11 scripts, 3 flip
  **Not one round that reported all gates green depends on which questions were asked** — bounded, by the rule of three on 0/60 cells, **below 0.050**. That is a bound, not a proof of impossibility.
  ⚠ **The strongest confound was checked, not assumed**: flippers do carry more gate rows (median 6 vs 4; Spearman(gate rows, flip rate) = +0.254), so more decision surfaces means more chances to flip. **But `OVERTURNED` rounds have the same median gate count as clean ones (4) and still flip at 0.073 — so gate count does not explain the separation.**
  ⚠ **The no-op floor is 0 flips out of 35**, so this is not formatting.
  ⇒ **One sentence about people: the worry was that a share of what this project says about people is really a statement about which twenty questions the questionnaire happened to contain. Measured across the corpus, that is true of one round in six — and every single one of them had already printed a verdict saying it was not sure.
  The rounds that claimed to have settled something had settled it independently of which questions were on the form. The ledger was already carrying the warning; nobody had ever checked that it was carrying it correctly.**
  ⚠ **A flip is a statement about MARGIN, never about truth** — a flipped round is not thereby wrong, and an unflipped one is not thereby right. This round ranks margin.
